extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working on Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory / arithmetic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Specifications and structural/compatibility requirements for building Hodge theatres, Frobenioids, and associated Kummer/cyclotomic data in inter-universal Teichmüller theory. Includes which cyclotomic rigidities to use where, and the required initial data and model objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity via LCFT (Cyc. Rig. LCFT2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cyclotomic rigidity obtained via local class field theory (LCFT). It is used for the constant monoids at local places in Vgood \ Vnon and is related with the local unit (modulo torsion) portion of the (theta)-links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rigidity for Kummer theory at local places in Vgood \ Vnon only. It essentially uses the value-group portion; therefore it is unsuitable at local places in Vbad where the value-group portion is deformed (it would render algorithms uniradial and only valid within a single Hodge theatre). It is compatible with the profinite topology. In Vgood \ Vnon one typically admits bZ(2)-indeterminacy (see related rubric) to make algorithms multiradial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environment (Cyc. Rig. Mono-th.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomic rigidity that arises from the mono-theta (mono-analytic theta) environment; employed for theta functions and their evaluations at local places in Vbad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rigidity for Kummer theory of theta functions/theta values at places in Vbad because it uses only the N-portion (the (·)N-portion) and does not rely on the value-group portion; thus it does not conflict with deformations of the value-group under (theta)-links and yields multiradial algorithms. It is compatible with the profinite topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity via Q>0 \ bZ(2) = {1} (Cyc. Rig. NF2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomic rigidity obtained by quotienting Q>0 by bZ(2) = {1}; used for non-realised global Frobenioids and related to the global realised portion of (theta)-links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rigidity for non-realised global Frobenioids / global aspects. It is multiradial but NOT compatible with the profinite topology: it has no natural ‘mod N’ finite-levels on the limit Kummer tower, so it is incompatible with log-links and cannot be transported under log-links. To construct log-links one must work at finite mod-N levels (compatibility with log-volumes appears only on realised Frobenioids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: do not use LCFT-cyclotomic rigidity at Vbad
rubrics_metrics.description: LCFT-based cyclotomic rigidity relies on the value-group portion; at local places in Vbad the value-group portion is deformed under (theta)-links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid applying LCFT rigidity for Kummer theory of theta functions/theta values at Vbad because the algorithm would be only valid inside the same Hodge theatre (uniradial). Instead, use the mono-theta environment rigidity at Vbad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of bZ(2)-indeterminacy in Vgood \ Vnon
rubrics_metrics.description: At local places in Vgood \ Vnon, only the unit portion is shared in (theta)-links while the value-group portion is not shared; to achieve multiradiality one admits bZ(2)-indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When employing LCFT rigidity in Vgood \ Vnon accept bZ(2)-indeterminacy so that algorithms become multiradial. This indeterminacy does not affect mono-analytic containers or local log-volumes in algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian transport: conjugacy and poly-action indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Mono-anabelian transport of certain objects (e.g., yM~) is obstructed because subgroups (CK) of the abstract topological group CF are only defined up to CF-conjugacy; one must consider F>_l-poly-action indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attempting mono-anabelian transport, account for indeterminacies arising from conjugacy (only defined up to normaliser action) and from nontrivial F>_l poly-actions. Work with yMmod (the yM~-invariant/trivial poly-acting part) if necessary to obtain objects without F>_l-indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with profinite topology (per rigidity type)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three cyclotomic rigidities differ in compatibility with the profinite (projective limit over ‘mod N’ levels) topology: LCFT and mono-theta are compatible; the Q>0\bZ rigidity is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Q>0\bZ rigidity lacks mod-N finite-level structure, it cannot be used for constructions that require passing to the pro-finite limit (e.g., log-links/logarithms on limits). Use LCFT or mono-theta where compatibility with profinite/projective-limit constructions is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: (theta)-line bundle ((cid:2)-line bundle) definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: (A (cid:2)-line bundle on (Spec O_K)==Gal(K/Fmod)) A (cid:2)-line bundle L(2) = (T; {t_v}_{v in V}) consists of: (a) T an F(2)_mod-torsor; (b) for each v in V a trivialisation t_v of the torsor T_v := T ⊗_{F(2)_mod} K_v(2) such that there exists t in T whose induced trivialisations agree with t_v for all but finitely many v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may define tensor powers L(2)^{	ens n} for n in Z. This structure is required when building Frobenioid line-bundles in the global-local set-up; finiteness of nontrivial local deviations is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of (cid:2)-line bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary morphism between (cid:2)-line bundles L1(2) = (T1,{t1_v}) and L2(2) = (T2,{t2_v}) is an isomorphism T1 -> T2 of F(2)_mod-torsors that sends each trivialisation t1_v to the F(2)_mod-orbit of t2_v (i.e., is integral at v). A general morphism is a pair (n>0, elementary morphism) describing a map L1(2) -> L2(2)^{	ens n}. Composites are defined in the obvious manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphisms must be integral at every v in V, and morphisms are considered up to the indicated tensor powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: (cid:1)-line bundle definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A (cid:1)-line bundle L(1) = {J_v}_{v in V} assigns to each v in V a fractional ideal J_v ⊂ K_v (finitely generated nonzero O_{K_v}-submodule for v in Vnon, and a positive real multiple of O_{K_v} for v in Varc) such that J_v = O_{K_v} for all but finitely many v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tensor powers L(1)^{	ens n} are defined in the obvious way. The finiteness condition (triviality at all but finitely many v) is required for global constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of (cid:1)-line bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary morphism between (cid:1)-line bundles L1(1) = {J1_v} and L2(1) = {J2_v} is an element f in F(2)_mod such that f * J1_v ⊂ J2_v (i.e., f is integral at v) for every v. A morphism is a pair (n>0, elementary morphism) corresponding to L1(1) -> L2(1)^{	ens n}. Compositions are defined naturally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrality at each place v is the required local condition for an elementary morphism; global morphisms are recorded along with an integer power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of a D-(cid:2)-Hodge theatre (required components)
rubrics_metrics.description: A D-(cid:2)-Hodge theatre consists of three portions: (local object) a holomorphic base-(or D-)prime-strip y_D^> = {y_{D^>;v}}_{v in V}, (local object) a capsule y_{D_J} = {y_{D_j}}_{j in J} of D-prime-strips indexed by J (J ≅ F^>_l), and (global object) a category y_D^} equivalent to B(C_K)^0; and two base-bridges: a base-(cid:2)-bridge connecting the capsule to the D-prime-strip y_D^>, and a base-(cid:2)-NF-bridge connecting the capsule to the global object y_D^}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each local holomorphic prime-strip must be of the prescribed shape depending on v (e.g., pv-adic Frobenioid for Vgood\Vnon, or Archimedean orbispace for Varc); the capsule is indexed by a finite approximation (F^>_l). The bridges provide the glueing data that place local objects over the global base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition / gluing of (cid:2)(cid:6)ellNF-Hodge theatre
rubrics_metrics.description: A (cid:2)(cid:6)ellNF-Hodge theatre is obtained by gluing a (cid:2)-NF-Hodge theatre (arithmetic part, with F^>_l-symmetry) and a (cid:2)(cid:6)ell-Hodge theatre (geometric part, with F0_l-symmetry) along appropriate base-objects; multiplicative (cid:2) and additive (cid:1) symmetries are separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation of multiplicative and additive symmetries in the gluing. The D-versions use torsor structures and specified Aut groups; ensure the appropriate torsor and bridge data (including D-bridges, NF-bridges, ell-bridges) are present and compatible with the base Hodge theatres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (1) — field and Galois setup
rubrics_metrics.description: F is a number field; write F̄ for an algebraic closure and G_F := Gal(F̄/F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fixes the global arithmetic base and notation for Galois actions used throughout the constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (2) — elliptic curve / punctured curve and moduli assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: X_F is a once-punctured elliptic curve over F with stable reduction over all v in V(F)non. Let E_F be the smooth compactification, C_F := X_F / {±1}, and let F_mod be the field of moduli (j-invariant). Assume F is Galois over F_mod of degree prime to l and that 2- and 3-torsion points of E_F are rational over F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions ensure control over torsion, moduli descent, and reduction behavior needed for the hyperbolic orbicurve and its Kummer/Frobenioid constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (3) — choice of V_bad (places of bad reduction) and related sets
rubrics_metrics.description: V_bad^{mod} ⊂ V^{mod} is non-empty such that X_F has bad (here multiplicative) reduction at places over V_bad^{mod}. Define V(F)_bad, V_non, V_arc, V_good etc. For v in V_bad, special structures (type (1; Z/lZ) orbicurve) are assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence and choice of V_bad and the partition of places into good/bad/archimedean/non-archimedean sets are essential to determine which rigidities and local models apply at each place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (4) — choice of prime l and Galois image
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a prime l ≥ 5 such that the image of the outer homomorphism G_F → GL2(F_l) from l-torsion contains SL2(F_l). Let K := F(E_F[l]). Require l to be coprime to degrees specified (e.g., not dividing places in V_bad^{mod} and not dividing q-parameter orders at V(F)_bad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures sufficiently large Galois image for torsion-level symmetry and that l is admissible relative to reduction data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (5) — orbicurve and hyperbolic type assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: C_F is a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1; l-tors). Let C_K be its K-core and X_K the associated hyperbolic curve type (1; l-tors). Existence of a uniquely determined open subgroup X^1_C giving the appropriate finite étale cover is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These geometric type assumptions fix the orbicurve/topological type used to define local/global Frobenioids and prime-strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (6) — choice of V as section of V(K)→V(mod) and local assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose V ⊂ V(K) mapping bijectively to V(mod). Define V_non, V_arc, V_good, V_bad accordingly. For v in V_bad assume the hyperbolic orbicurve C_v is of type (1; Z/lZ); for v in V write specific local temp/Frobenioid models X_v and (temp) prime categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Picking V as an analytic section identifies local places over K with moduli places and supplies the required local models and cusp identifications used in Hodge theatre constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (cid:2)-data: condition (7) — choice and properties of the cusp
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix a non-zero cusp c of the hyperbolic orbicurve C_K. For each v in V the local cusp c_v is the one determined by c. For v in V_bad require that c_v arises from the canonical generator (up to sign) of bZ via the natural surjection of the tempered fundamental group to bZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consistent choice of cusp across places (and its relation to the canonical bZ-generator at bad places) is required to define theta-functions, q-parameters, and the canonical multiplicative subspace phenomena used in the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local model objects (Definition of D_v, D'_v, C_v, F_v, C'_v, F'_v)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each v in V one must choose appropriate local model categories and Frobenioid-theoretic objects: D_v (holomorphic base category depending on v-type), D'_v (mono-analytic base), C_v (holomorphic Frobenioid-theoretic hull), F_v (tempered/p-adic/Archimedean Frobenioid), C'_v and F'_v (mono-analytic/p-adic split versions) according to whether v ∈ V_bad, V_good\V_non, or V_arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assignment depends on the place-type and must be made coherently so that natural equivalences and splittings exist between the mono-analytic and holomorphic/p-adic/Archimedean versions; these model objects are used to form prime-strips and Hodge-theatre local pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model global objects (D^} = B(C_K)^0 and D^}(cid:6) = B(X_K)^0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the global model categories D^} := B(C_K)^0 and D^}(cid:6) := B(X_K)^0 to serve as the global objects over which local objects are to be consistently labelled and glued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphs of these global objects are used to write consistent labels on local objects; they act as the global base for D-(cid:2)- and D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global realised Frobenioid with localisations (model and log-volume data)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a global realised Frobenioid C^{(13)}_{mod} together with a bijection of primes Prime(C^{(13)}_{mod}) ↔ V_mod and localisation maps to local realiﬁcations C'_v, giving elements log'_v determined up to specified scaling factors (e.g., [K_v:(F_mod)_v] factors). The global theta-monoid and its localisations (with formal log((cid:2)) symbols) are defined accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This global-to-local compatibility of monoids/log-elements is used to define log-volume functions and to compare log-data across places; the precise normalisation factors must be respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: (cid:2)-version model constructions for v-cases (Deﬁnition 10.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each place-type (V_bad, V_good\V_non, V_arc) there are concrete prescriptions for building the local pv-adic or Archimedean Frobenioid objects (monoids O^3_{C^{(2)}_v}, formal log symbols, split pre-Frobenioids, and splittings) and for producing corresponding (cid:2)-objects and split pre-Frobenioids. Natural equivalences with the mono-analytic objects must be exhibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the place-dependent recipes: e.g., in V_bad construct O^3 using connected temperoid objects and projections; in V_good \ V_non include formal symbols log(p_v) log((2)); in Varc replace divisor monoid image by R_{>0} and include formal symbols. Ensure the splitting/compatibility data (spl(cid:2), spl') are provided and coherent with the global realisation.
